newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arnotts starts dumping recalled stock.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arnotts starts dumping recalled stock.

text.p: Australian biscuit company Arnotts Ltd on Friday began dumping millions of packets of biscuits cleared from retail shelves after an extortion threat.
Arnotts said in a statement it believed none of the stock was contaminated, but was being "ultra-safe".
Also, much of the stock being dumped at a tip at Eastern Creek in western Sydney was damaged when it was removed from shops in Queensland and New South Wales on February 14, it said.
Arnotts managing director Chris Roberts said no returned stock would be sent back to shops.
"Only new stock will go onto the shelves ... when the company believes it is appropriate to do so," he said in a statement.
Police on Wednesday called on an extortionist who has threatened to plant poisoned biscuits in supermarkets to contact them by next Monday or they would consider the threat ended.

The extortionist had threatened to plant pesticide-laced Arnotts biscuits in the two states from Monday this week, but there have been no reports of poisoned biscuits or any further communications from the extortionist.
The extortionist wanted police involved in a 1991 murder case to take a lie detector test in the claimed belief that a man serving a jail sentence for the murder had been framed.
Arnotts, a 70 percent owned subsidiary of U.S. food giant Campbell Soup Co, has said it will lose A$5.0 million a week in sales due to the recall.
